title: Communities In Schools of Laredo Marks 35 Years of Keeping Students in School
excerpt: Communities In Schools of Laredo is celebrating 35 years of serving students and families in Webb County, having worked with 25,000 students through school-based partnerships, counseling, tutoring and mentoring since its founding in 1989, according to the Laredo Morning Times.
content:
Communities In Schools (CIS) of Laredo is celebrating 35 years of serving students and families in Webb County, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Founded in 1989, CIS runs year-round programs in elementary, middle and high schools to help students stay in school, succeed and graduate. Its mission is to surround students with a community of support, empowering them to stay in school and achieve in life, the newspaper reported.

The Laredo organization is part of the Communities In Schools of America national network, which serves 2 million students a year, and of the Texas state CIS network. It has worked with 25,000 students through school-based partnerships, counseling, tutoring, mentoring and more, according to the article.

CIS supports the whole child with academic support, mental health referrals, transportation support, hygiene products, food assistance, career exploration and college readiness, along with help building skills and confidence. Its programs also address whole-family needs, including emergency support, parent education and basic-needs assistance, the newspaper reported.

Many young people who benefited from CIS return to serve as mentors and volunteers, the article noted. Its executive director, Dr. Alicia G. Tijerina, wrote that after 35 years beside students and families, the organization's commitment is stronger than ever, and that with the support of schools, partners and the community, it will keep showing up for the young people who need it most.

The anniversary is also a call to action, the article said: readers are urged to get involved, volunteer, donate and encourage a young person.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 14, 2026.
